# Records you need to keep
## How long to keep your records
You must keep your written evidence for **5 years** from the date you lodge your tax return.

- 5 years from the date of your last claim for decline in value, if you claim a deduction for the decline in value of depreciating assets
- for the later of the following periods if you're in dispute with us, either
  - 5 years from the date you lodge your tax return

web.description:
- The ATO requires you to keep business records for **five years from the date you lodge** your tax return for the relevant income year.

## The 5-Year Rule (and When It Does Not Apply)
The foundational ATO record keeping directive specifies retaining documents for **five years from the date you lodge your tax return** for the relevant income year.

The five-year clock commences from the **lodgement date**, not the transaction date.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### How long do I need to keep tax records in Australia?
The ATO requires five-year retention from the lodgement date for the relevant income year.

### Is the ATO record keeping requirement 5 years or 7 years?
Standard ATO requirement is five years from lodgement date.
